**Stubbing:** [Btw saying you're not good as leadership is a classic humility move and makes us enlightened Losers more eager to follow you into the pits o](https://venkateshrao.com/blyg/t/7qwq5fnqg1cneeg11nd5tgp0cg/)

So I used to be a community organizer in the Saul Alinsky tradition. Not for very long, but that is something I did once upon a time, oh so long ago.

These kinds of organizers **thought a lot about leadership** because that was the theory of organizing they pursued: You didn't organize people; you organized the people who already had people organized.

This tradition of community work had a really succinct definition of leadership: **A leader is a person that has followers.**

* That is, there are any number of people who will tend to show up when that person asks, they are a leader. Full stop.

The critique they were making here is that a lot of people talk about what makes a leader a leader. But thesse organizers had found that those lists of characteristics never really fit on the ground. If you just dropped all those expectations of what a leader ought to look like and just looked around to see which people other people were listening to, then you would find a lot more leaders.
